next_step: Run 1-week POC: streaming latency tests + tool-calling smoke tests; finalize pricing delta; schedule procurement sync w/ finance
notes: Background: mid-market SaaS (customer support platform) with hosted multi-tenant product used by SMBs and some enterprise customers.
Primary ask: replace brittle bot infra with hosted LLM for live chat agents + assistive suggestions. Want streaming responses and function/tool-calling to Zendesk and our internal KB microservice.

Latency SLO: business requires <1.5s first-token for NA users; engineering aiming for <1.2s median first-token under typical load (200 concurrent active chats peak). Streaming is mandatory for perceived responsiveness.
Current approach: evaluating Hosted API first to shorten time-to-value, then consider Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable latency and lower unit cost if POC successful.

POC plan: 1-week hosted POC. Tests: 1) first-token latency across regions (us-east-1/us-west-2), 2) streaming bandwidth and reassembly, 3) tool-calling flows to Zendesk (create/update ticket) and KB lookup, 4) throughput under 150-250 concurrent sessions.

Security: SOC2 required; SSO/SAML for admin console; audit logs and KMS integration mandatory; retention: ask is 30 days for transcripts but legal pushing for configurable retention and exportability.
Cost sensitivity: finance worried about per-token costs at scale; interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations and quantization guidance. Potential to commit to Dedicated if unit economics justify.
Integrations: want function calling + structured output (JSON) to avoid brittle parsing. Need examples of OpenAPI/tool-call snippets and best practices for idempotency when creating tickets.
Quote from Head of Product: "Users bail if the first response feels slow — streaming is a must. We need consistent sub-1.5s first token across peak hours."
Technical asks from Eng lead: kernel selection/latency profile for 2k prompt max, KV cache expectations for chat continuity, ability to pin model versions during rollout.

Recent asks: security questionnaire submitted (drive/Threadline_Security_FAQ). Asked for SOC2 cert, data flow diagram, and customer responsibility matrix. SE asked to provide sample streaming SDK snippet and benchmark harness.

Risk areas: legal delay on retention clause, SSO cert exchange timing, and Zendesk OAuth token scope for ticket creation. Procurement needs a pricing slide that shows hosted-to-dedicated migration economics.
Positive signals: product liked Redwood's streaming SDK and model routing/fallback demo. Customer excited about automatic prefix caching mention in demo — could reduce token count on long threads.
Internal notes: AE to share Redwood POC template + benchmark script. SE to instrument the POC with real-traffic mirrors (anonymized) for realistic latency numbers.
Expected timeline: POC kickoff 2026-03-08, POC end 2026-03-14, procurement decision window mid-April 2026.
